title: Uniform-Charge-Density $d$-Wave Superconductivity in the Pure $t$-$J$ Model at $1/8$ Doping on an Infinite Cylinder
abstract: The ground state of the square-lattice $t$-$J$ model at $1/8$ hole doping has been the subject of a long-standing controversy, with conflicting numerical reports of stripe order versus superconductivity. Here, we address this debate using the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) method, which optimizes the wave function directly in the thermodynamic limit along the cylinder axis and eliminates the boundary pinning effects that can arise in finite-cylinder calculations. On an infinite cylinder of circumference $L_y = 8$, we find a uniform-charge-density $d$-wave superconducting ground state with quasi-long-range pairing correlations. The dominant pairing occurs at zero center-of-mass momentum, while no sizable finite-momentum pairing component is detected. Twisted-boundary-condition calculations reveal a finite superconducting phase stiffness, with the order-parameter phase winding smoothly to follow the applied flux, providing an independent probe of the robustness of the superconductivity. Moreover, both charge and spin correlations decay rapidly, with no signatures of long-range stripe or magnetic order, in contrast to an $L_y=6$ cylinder at $1/6$ doping where the same method readily identifies stripe order. Our results provide methodologically distinct evidence in the long-standing stripe--superconductivity debate in the pure $t$-$J$ model and reveal uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in a minimal model of doped Mott insulators.
summary: This theoretical study uses the VUMPS method on the $t$-$J$ model to resolve the stripe vs. superconductivity debate at 1/8 doping. The authors conclude that the system favors a uniform $d$-wave superconducting state, as evidenced by robust pairing correlations and the rapid decay of charge and spin order parameters. This provides methodologically distinct evidence supporting superconductivity in this minimal model.
main_problem: The paper addresses the long-standing controversy regarding the ground state of the $t$-$J$ model at $1/8$ hole doping, specifically whether it exhibits stripe order or superconductivity.
main_result: The study finds that the ground state is a uniform-charge-density $d$-wave superconductor with quasi-long-range pairing correlations, while charge and spin correlations decay rapidly, ruling out long-range stripe or magnetic order.
method: The Variational Uniform Matrix Product State (VUMPS) method is employed to optimize the wave function in the thermodynamic limit along the cylinder axis.
model_or_system: The system is the pure $t$-$J$ model on a square lattice, studied at $1/8$ hole doping ($\langle n_i angle = 0.875$). The analysis is performed on an infinite cylinder geometry.
key_observables: Superconducting pairing ($\Delta$), superconducting phase stiffness, charge structure factor ($N(\mathbf{k})$), spin structure factor ($S(\mathbf{k})$), and real-space correlation functions ($\langle n_i n_{i+r} angle_c$, $\langle S_i \cdot S_{i+r} angle$).
main_assumptions: The VUMPS method eliminates boundary pinning effects, and the rapid decay of correlations is robust across different fitting parametrizations.
figures_summary: Figures show the $d$-wave structure of the order parameter, confirmation of quasi-long-range pairing via power-law decay of correlations, and the absence of sharp peaks in charge/spin structure factors on the $L_y=8$ cylinder.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes superconducting order (via pairing correlations and phase stiffness), then investigates charge and spin correlations (via structure factors and real-space decay), contrasting the results with known stripe-forming regimes (e.g., $L_y=6$ at $1/6$ doping).
why_interesting: The rigorous application of advanced tensor network methods to resolve fundamental debates in strongly correlated electron systems provides crucial benchmarks for understanding high-Tc superconductivity mechanisms.
